scenario: One router r1 has two data ports joined by a same-router wire. Add a service endpoint and two planned static routes, then admit the approved aggregate contributor while rejecting the other, keeping the rejected aggregate as a hidden route.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a mask other than /32 or another interface
commonMistakes.recognise: show route 192.0.2.2 shows no Direct /32 entry

explanation: A /32 on lo0.0 creates a Direct 192.0.2.2/32 route; a different mask would create a different Direct prefix, so the route check pins the mask.
stages.goal: Make lo0.0 carry service address 192.0.2.2 with an exact host mask, reachable from r1.
stages.hint: Use the interface address with a host-length mask and compare the interface and route views.

r1: set interfaces lo0 unit 0 family inet address 192.0.2.2/32

stages.title: Establish the exact local service endpoint

commonMistakes.recognise: show route forwarding-table destination for each prefix
commonMistakes.symptom: Forwarding entry shows rjct for 172.16.10.0/24 or dscd for 172.17.10.0/24

doneWhen: 172.16.10.0/24 is active Static with a discard forwarding entry
172.17.10.0/24 is active Static with a reject forwarding entry
explanation: Forwarding table next-hop types dscd and rjct show the difference between discard and reject.
stages.goal: Create the two planned networks as static routes, one that silently drops traffic and one that drops it with an error response.
stages.hint: Compare the forwarding table entries of the two prefixes.
stages.title: Represent the two planned networks

commonMistakes.recognise: show route 172.17.0.0/16 shows an active Aggregate and the hidden view is empty
commonMistakes.symptom: Aggregate stays active in the ordinary view
Prefix is absent from the hidden view too

doneWhen: 172.17.0.0/16 is absent from the ordinary route view but present as Aggregate in the hidden view
explanation: A policy accepting only 172.16.10.0/24 gives 172.16.0.0/16 a contributor; 172.17.10.0/24 is rejected, and with no passive property the 172.17.0.0/16 aggregate has no contributor so it is hidden.
stages.goal: Activate aggregate 172.16.0.0/16 using only the approved contributor, and make aggregate 172.17.0.0/16 inactive through contributor policy while keeping its definition.
stages.hint: Compare show route and show route hidden for both aggregates.

r1: set policy-options policy-statement AGG-CONTRIB term approved from route-filter 172.16.10.0/24 exact
set policy-options policy-statement AGG-CONTRIB term approved then accept
set policy-options policy-statement AGG-CONTRIB term other then reject
set routing-options aggregate route 172.16.0.0/16 policy AGG-CONTRIB
set routing-options aggregate route 172.17.0.0/16 policy AGG-CONTRIB

stages.title: Distinguish rejected contribution from route deletion

r1: set interfaces lo0 unit 0 family inet address 192.0.2.1/32

startState.description: r1 has ge-0/0/0 and ge-0/0/1 up/up and 192.0.2.1/32 on lo0.0. Aggregate 172.17.0.0/16 is configured as passive, so it is active in the ordinary route view and absent from the hidden view. Service 192.0.2.2/32, the two statics and aggregate 172.16.0.0/16 are absent.

summary: Configure an exact loopback service address, two static routes with different forwarding actions, and aggregate contributor policy on one router. Fixed values: service 192.0.2.2/32 on lo0.0; discard route 172.16.10.0/24; reject route 172.17.10.0/24; approved contributor 172.16.10.0/24; aggregates 172.16.0.0/16 and 172.17.0.0/16.
title: Local Addressing, Static Routes, and Contributor Policy
